The search results mostly come from vendor pages and comparison blogs, so treat the figures as unverified. Here's what they say:

**Shared IPs and dedicated IPs:** Both platforms use shared IPs by default and sell dedicated IPs as an add-on. Postmark's own page argues its shared pools have a longer track record, which it says has been managed for over a decade. ([postmarkapp.com](https://postmarkapp.com/compare/resend-alternative))

**Dedicated IP thresholds and cost:** One comparison says Postmark dedicated IPs require 300,000+ emails per month at $50 each, and that below that volume a dedicated IP can hurt deliverability by lacking traffic to build reputation. ([toolradar.com](https://toolradar.com/compare/postmark-vs-resend-mcp)) Resend's migration page, a competitor's claim, says Postmark charges $50 per dedicated IP and Resend charges $30. ([resend.com](https://resend.com/migrate/postmark)) Resend reportedly offers dedicated IPs only on its Scale plans. ([nuntly.com](https://nuntly.com/versus/resend-vs-postmark))

**Message streams:** Postmark separates transactional and broadcast mail into distinct streams, so a promotional campaign never shares IP reputation with transactional receipts. ([wpmailsmtp.com](https://wpmailsmtp.com/postmark-review/)) One comparison says Resend does not enforce this separation. ([nuntly.com](https://nuntly.com/versus/resend-vs-postmark))

**Inbox placement figures:** One 2026 guide cites a 98.7% inbox placement rate and 1.2-second average delivery for Postmark, but I found no independent source confirming these numbers. ([apiscout.dev](https://apiscout.dev/blog/resend-vs-postmark-api-2026)) Postmark also publishes live delivery-time data for the last 30–60 days, which is self-reported. ([postmarkapp.com](https://postmarkapp.com/compare/resend-alternative))

**Other differences:** Postmark keeps logs for 45 days versus Resend's 3 days, and Postmark supports inbound parsing while Resend doesn't. ([nuntly.com](https://nuntly.com/versus/resend-vs-postmark), [sequenzy.com](https://sequenzy.com/versus/resend-vs-postmark))

**Bottom line:** Postmark has the stronger deliverability reputation and stream separation, according to these sources. Resend has the more generous free tier and a React Email workflow. Neither source set I found provides independent, head-to-head inbox placement testing, so verify with your own seed-list or pilot tests before deciding.

## Transactional Plans

| Plan | Price | Emails/mo | Overage (per 1,000) | Custom Domains | Data Retention | Dedicated IPs | Webhook Endpoints |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Free | $0 | 3,000 | None | 3 | 30 days | No | 1 |
| Pro | $20 | 50,000 | $0.90 | 10 (+100 with $20/mo add-on) | 30 days | No | 5 |
| Pro | $35 | 100,000 | $0.90 | 10 (+100 with add-on) | 30 days | No | 5 |
| Scale | $90 | 100,000 | $0.90 | 1,000 (+100 with add-on) | 30 days | $30/mo add-on, for senders over 3,000/day | 10 |
| Scale | $160 | 200,000 | $0.80 | 1,000 (+100 with add-on) | 30 days | Same as above | 10 |
| Scale | $350 | 500,000 | $0.70 | 1,000 (+100 with add-on) | 30 days | Same as above | 10 |
| Scale | $650 | 1,000,000 | $0.65 | 1,000 (+100 with add-on) | 30 days | Same as above | 10 |
| Scale | $825 | 1,500,000 | $0.52 | 1,000 (+100 with add-on) | 30 days | Same as above | 10 |
| Scale | $1,150 | 2,500,000 | $0.46 | 1,000 (+100 with add-on) | 30 days | Same as above | 10 |
| Enterprise | Custom | Custom | Custom | Flexible | Flexible | Listed as add-on, but also as included (see note) | Flexible |

**Other limits:**
- **Daily sending:** Free is capped at 100 emails/day. Pro, Scale, and Enterprise have no daily limit.
- **API rate limit:** The FAQ says requests per second are the same on every plan, so upgrading doesn't raise it. The feature list also mentions "Enterprise rate limits," which the FAQ doesn't explain.
- **Overage:** Free has none. Paid plans can enable pay-as-you-go, billed in 1,000-email blocks.

## Deliverability Features by Tier

- **Free:** Shared IPs, DKIM/SPF/DMARC, automatic suppression list, bounce details, deliverability insights, multi-region. No deliverability expertise, dedicated IPs, or warmup.
- **Pro:** Everything in Free, plus personalized deliverability recommendations based on your sending.
- **Scale:** Everything in Pro, plus dedicated IPs (add-on) with automatic warmup, Slack support, and an urgent response SLA.
- **Enterprise:** Everything in Scale, plus a 99.99% uptime SLA, flexible retention, and flexible domain and webhook limits.

**Note:** The sources conflict on Enterprise dedicated IPs. The comparison table lists them as an add-on, while the Enterprise and marketing sections say they're included.

## Marketing Plans (Contact-Based)

Marketing plans aren't capped by emails sent, only by contacts:
- **Free:** 1,000 contacts, no dedicated IPs.
- **Pro marketing:** $40 to $650/mo for 5,000 to 150,000 contacts. Dedicated IPs are available as an add-on.
- **Enterprise:** Custom pricing, with dedicated IPs included.

# Resend vs Postmark for transactional email

**I recommend Postmark if deliverability and reliability matter most. Choose Resend if cost, a generous free tier, or developer experience matter most.** The numbers below come from the vendors' pricing pages, fetched today. The comparison claims come from third-party blogs and vendor marketing, so treat them as unverified.

## Pricing

| | **Resend** | **Postmark** |
|---|---|---|
| Free | 3,000/mo (100/day cap), 3 domains | 100/mo |
| Entry paid | $20 for 50k, or $35 for 100k | From $15 for 10k (Basic) |
| Mid-tier | Scale: $90 for 100k, $350 for 500k | Pro from $16.50 for 10k, Platform from $18 for 10k |
| Overage per 1,000 | $0.90 (Pro), falling to $0.46 (Scale) | $1.80 (Basic), $1.30 (Pro), $1.20 (Platform) |
| Dedicated IP | $30/mo add-on, Scale plan only, for senders over 3,000/day | $50/mo per IP, Pro or higher, aimed at 300k+/mo |
| Log retention | 30 days | 45 days (Basic), customizable up to 365 days on Pro and above |

At 50k emails a month, Resend costs about $20. Postmark would be roughly $65–75, because its tiers scale from 10k and the overage is higher. I estimated that from its per-1,000 overage rates, and the page doesn't list a 50k price. Resend is much cheaper at low and mid volume.

## Deliverability
- **Both:**
  - Shared IPs by default, with dedicated IPs as a paid add-on.
  - DKIM/SPF/DMARC support.
  - Automatic suppression lists.
- **Resend:**
  - Bounce details and deliverability insights on every plan.
  - Personalized deliverability recommendations on Pro.
  - Dedicated IPs with automatic warmup on Scale.
- **Postmark:**
  - Separate message streams for transactional and broadcast mail, so promotional sends don't affect transactional reputation. This comes from a [Postmark review](https://wpmailsmtp.com/postmark-review/). A [competitor comparison](https://nuntly.com/versus/resend-vs-postmark) says Resend doesn't enforce this separation.
  - Inbound email processing on Pro and above.
  - An optional DMARC monitoring add-on, from $14/mo per domain.
  - A long reputation for fast delivery and strict sender vetting. [One guide](https://apiscout.dev/blog/resend-vs-postmark-api-2026) cites 98.7% inbox placement, but I found no independent confirmation.

## Caveats
- I found no independent head-to-head inbox-placement test. Run a pilot with a seed-list tool such as GlockApps against your own domain and content.
- Resend's pricing page lists 30-day retention, while a comparison blog says 3 days. I'd trust the pricing page.
- Resend's pricing page contradicts itself on whether Enterprise includes dedicated IPs. Postmark's Free-tier retention is also inconsistent.
- Dedicated IPs are rarely worth buying below about 100–300k emails a month. Stay on shared IPs until you reach that volume.

## Recommendation
- **Choose Postmark** if the emails are business-critical (password resets, receipts, 2FA), if you want long log retention, inbound parsing, or stream separation, and if a higher per-email cost is acceptable.
- **Choose Resend** if you're early-stage or cost-sensitive, you value the API and React Email workflow, or your volume is modest. The 3,000/mo free tier makes it easy to start.

Since you asked for one pick: **Postmark**, because deliverability is the point of transactional email and its track record and stream separation are the stronger evidence. If you expect to stay under about 50k/mo on a tight budget, starting on Resend is reasonable. Both have simple APIs, so switching later is cheap.

Sources:
- [Resend pricing](https://resend.com/pricing)
- [Postmark pricing](https://postmarkapp.com/pricing)
- [Postmark: Resend alternative](https://postmarkapp.com/compare/resend-alternative)
- [Resend: migrate from Postmark](https://resend.com/migrate/postmark)
- [Nuntly comparison](https://nuntly.com/versus/resend-vs-postmark)
- [WPMailSMTP Postmark review](https://wpmailsmtp.com/postmark-review/)
- [APIScout 2026 comparison](https://apiscout.dev/blog/resend-vs-postmark-api-2026)
- [Toolradar comparison](https://toolradar.com/compare/postmark-vs-resend-mcp)
